Martin Henig suggests that the pattern of apparently random grooves seen on the Colchester example maybe derived from the human figure. The poorly executed image on this ring may show a bird holding a branch. This ring…

epigrafe.descrizione: A Roman hooked harness mount. The mount has a circular domed body, concave on the back, with a pair of rounded side projections and a large central knop. A small hook with a rounded end emerges from the lower side of the dome. From the other side emerges a pelta-shaped plate with an inscribed branching or herring-bone pattern. An integral rivet projects from the back of the plate

epigrafe.descrizione: Four irregular-shaped lumps of lead-alloy, each of which contains one or more late Roman nummi. Two pieces were discovered in context, and the other two were discovered in the plough soil nearby. An illegible late Roman nummus was discovered loose next to this lump.…

epigrafe.provenienza: contea di ritrovamento: Lincolnshire (Inghilterra e Galles)
epigrafe.descrizione: A cast copper-alloy finger ring of Guiraud type 2, dating c . 43-250. The finger ring has a round hoop and flattened bezel, with shoulders tapering from the bezel into the hoop. In section the hoop is D-shaped. The bezel is inscribed with a simple depiction of a quadruped animal standing to the right. Small lines down its spine probably indicated bristles, suggesting that the animal is a boar

There is some moulded decoration across the breadth of the head, but no stamp or inscription. The bow has a central ridge decorated with a band containing raised…

epigrafe.descrizione: A copper alloy Roman brooch, probably an Aucissa type. The bow has a raised rib along the centre, making it triangular in section and is otherwise undecorated. It terminates in a globular foot. The wings, catch plate and pin are all mostly missing; and the bow has been bent in antiquity. The head of the brooch appears always to have been flat, probably with a small rolled area to hold the axis…

The spring is held in the topmost of two perforations in a lug which…

epigrafe.descrizione: Silver republican denarius, minted between 32 - 31 BC (Reece Period 1) by M. Antonius, Mint: moving with the moneyer. Reverse Legend: LEG XV. epigrafe.provenienza: contea di ritrovamento: Worcestershire (Inghilterra e Galles)
epigrafe.descrizione: A rectangular strip of lead that has carefully and deliberately been folded in half. The object is just possibly a Roman curse tablet, although it may well be more modern and may have performed an entirely different function, perhaps such as a weight. If it is a curse tablet it may have an inscription on the interior requesting assistance from a deity. However, curse tablets do tend to be folded…

epigrafe.descrizione: A Roman silver coin: a denarius of Nerva dating from AD 96 - 98 (Reece period 5), reverse legend AEQVITAS AVGVST, depicting Aequitas standing, facing left, holding scales and cornucopia. Rome mint. Reference: Sear, volume 2, number 3019 and RIC II no. 25. Compare BH-E4D017 . The coin is 17.1mm in diameter and 2.1mm thick. It weighs 2.68gm
